newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down but holds chart range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down but holds chart range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended lower across the board Thursday in a moderate session, but forecasts for colder Northeast weather next week tempered the selling and held prices within recent ranges.
April slipped 1.3 cents to close at $1.942 per million British thermal units. May settled 1.1 cents lower at $2.017. Other deferreds ended down by 0.8 to four cents.

"It's been a clash between fundamentals and technicals. Fundamentals say the market looks terrible, but technicals say it doesn't look too bad, but we're still on the high side of the range," said one Houston-based trader.

While forecasts for colder Northeast weather this week and next tempered the bears, most agreed ample storage and typically-weak spring demand were likely to make any rally a struggle. And some said producing region injections, which were expected in AGA data this week and helped buoy the cash, could undermine prices later in the month.

"Cash has been relatively strong which means gas is going in the ground, but that's not bullish longer-term. It just means that if cash tries to spike, they (storage buyers) will be able to say no," the Houston-trader said.

Technical traders still pegged resistance in April at $2.04, then in the mid-teens and at $2.28. Support was seen at $1.88, with better buying expected at $1.78-1.80 and then at the $1.701 contract low.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed a couple of cents Thursday to the mid-$1.90s. Midcon pipes gained more than a nickel to the low-$1.90s. New York city gate swing gas also rose slightly to the mid-to-high $2.20s.
The 12-month strip gained 1.8 cents to $2.133. NYMEX said an estimated 27,451 contracts traded, down from Wednesday's revised tally of 31,699.
NYMEX Permian and Alberta natgas did not trade Thursday.
On the KCBT, April finished 0.1 cent lower at $1.719, while most deferreds ended steady to down one cent. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.2 cents to 22.3 cents (NYMEX premium).
